what: My reading of the reasons the reviewers gave for marking a passage Misleading (not a mark by anyone else, and not a lawyer's reading). Re-made on 2026-10-09 after the two missing ChatGPT replies (R02, R06) arrived: 34 passages, 4 new (R02 #1, R02 #3, R06 #5, R06 #7).

classes.R: a later ruling or statute replaced what the passage says
classes.S: records a lawyer's or a party's submission, not the court's holding

R02#1.why: counsel's submission opposing electronic service, not the Court's holding (ChatGPT)

R02#3.why: a submission advocating personal service, not adopted as the holding (ChatGPT)

R02#4.why: the State's argument for electronic service, which the Court rejects (ChatGPT, Gemini A and B)

R02#8.why: a lawyer's submission, not the Court's holding (ChatGPT A and B, Gemini B)

R04#3.why: the earlier limited-duration approach that the Constitution Bench in the same judgment rejects (all runs)

R04#5.why: counsel's submissions against limiting anticipatory bail (ChatGPT A and B)

R06#5.why: a party's argument for entitlement under section 479, not a holding (ChatGPT)

R06#7.why: about the former section 436A and rejects its direct application; does not decide the BNSS 479 question (ChatGPT)

R09#2.why: old view on the payee's bank, superseded by the 2015 amendment of section 142(2) and later rulings (Gemini)

R09#5.why: rule contrary to the account-based jurisdiction rule the later statute set (ChatGPT, Gemini)

R09#8.why: jurisdiction on presentation alone, which conflicts with the statutory account-based rule (ChatGPT)

R11#1.why: Kanhaiyalal: NCB statements as confessions, overruled by Tofan Singh (all runs)

R11#4.why: Kanhaiyalal line: section 67 confession alone sustains conviction, contrary to Tofan Singh (all runs)

R11#6.why: Binda (2023) recounting the earlier admissibility position, no longer good law after Tofan Singh (all runs)

R11#7.why: recounts an earlier case's question and arguments; the earlier approach conflicts with the later ruling (one run; mixed with S)

R11#9.why: repeats the Kanhaiyalal rule without the later rejection (all runs)

R11#10.why: pre-Tofan Singh view that statements to narcotics officers sustain a conviction (ChatGPT A, Gemini A and B)

R11#11.why: states the earlier rule rejected by Tofan Singh (all runs)

R11#12.why: a Tofan Singh passage that reproduces the earlier position without the controlling prohibition (one run)

R11#14.why: Central Bureau of Narcotics confessions admissible, the superseded view (all runs)

R14#7.why: reproduces the complainant's fraud allegations, which could be read as a finding (ChatGPT)

R14#13.why: the respondent's counsel's argument against quashing (ChatGPT, Gemini)

R14#15.why: a different construction-business dispute whose quashing contentions failed (ChatGPT)

R15#1.why: the Family Welfare Committee and no-arrest direction later declared impermissible (ChatGPT)

R15#7.why: the committee and no-arrest directions later declared impermissible (ChatGPT)

R15#9.why: the no-arrest direction, with the committee directions later declared impermissible (ChatGPT)

R20#4.why: a slip in the Court's own text says 'complainant' for 'accused' (Gemini)

R21#6.why: Shafhi Mohammad, overruled by Arjun Panditrao (ChatGPT, Gemini)

R21#7.why: Shafhi Mohammad argument later overruled by a larger bench (ChatGPT, Gemini; mixed with S)

R21#8.why: Shafhi Mohammad approach later overruled (ChatGPT, Gemini)

R22#5.why: rejects family circumstances as a ground to reduce a death sentence; could mislead if read alone (ChatGPT, Gemini)

R26#10.why: counsel's submissions, not the Court's holding (ChatGPT)

R28#8.why: reports a rejected waiver and the limits of Article 142; could suggest the waiting period can never be waived (ChatGPT A and B, Gemini)
